article_title: Dominant misconceptions and alluvial flows between Engineering and Physical Science students
citation: Anna Chrysostomou, Alan S. Cornell, and Wade Naylor. (2024). Dominant misconceptions and alluvial flows between Engineering and Physical Science students. https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2133-7924
title: Normalised dominant misconception (nDM) measure with a 50% threshold for identifying dominant incorrect FCI responses without paired data
description: The nDM is a normalisation of the largest incorrect FCI answer choice, computed per question from five options plus non-attempt (NA), with a threshold (chosen as 50% here, following Martín-Blas et al. and Bani-Salameh) above which an incorrect choice is deemed dominant. The article states "this normalisation allows for the identification of DMs even in the absence of paired data". It amplifies misconceptions drowned out by correct answers and exposes subdominant ones, and can be applied at pre-test alone.
requirements: Requires a chosen threshold percentage for classifying an incorrect answer as dominant; a FCI-style instrument with a known correct answer per question.
constraints: Part of the apparent post-test increase in % nDM is by design, since % correct is subtracted in the normalisation denominator; some questions have no DM and some may have more than one dominant incorrect choice.
target_learners: first-year university Engineering and Physical Science students
target_learning_goals: diagnosing conceptual understanding of Newtonian mechanics
examples: Applied to 2022 UJ BEng. and BPhys. FCI cohorts, and compared against Spanish and KSA pre-test nDM data in Table 6
key_sources: Anna Chrysostomou, Alan S. Cornell, and Wade Naylor. (2024). Dominant misconceptions and alluvial flows between Engineering and Physical Science students. https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2133-7924
